questions.q: What were some of the last things David did as king of Israel?
questions.a: David made Solomon king in his place, and he counted the Levites who were at least 30 years old.

questions.q: What jobs did David give to the Levites?
questions.a: He divided them into groups of overseers of the work of Yahweh’s house, officers and judges, gatekeepers, and others to praise Yahweh with instruments.

questions.q: Who were the sons of Gershon?
questions.a: The sons of Gershon were Ladan and Shimei.

questions.q: Who were the sons of Ladan and Shimei?
questions.a: Ladan’s sons were Jehiel, Zetham, and Joel. Shimei’s sons were Shelomoth, Haziel, and Haran, and they were leaders of Ladan’s clans.

questions.q: Who were the other four sons of Shimei, and how were two of them counted?
questions.a: Shimei’s other sons were Jahath, Zina, Jeush, and Beriah. Because Jeush and Beriah did not have many sons, they were counted together as one clan.

questions.q: Who were the sons of Kohath?
questions.a: Kohath’s sons were Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.

questions.q: What were Aaron and his descendants chosen to do permanently?
questions.a: Aaron and his descendants were chosen to work in the most holy place, to offer sacrifices to Yahweh, to serve him, and to praise him forever.

questions.q: Although Moses was a man of God, how were his descendants counted, and who were his two sons?
questions.a: Moses’s descendants were counted as Levites, not as priests. His sons were Gershom and Eliezer.

questions.q: Who were the sons of Merari, and what happened to Eleazar’s children?
questions.a: Merari’s sons were Mahli and Mushi, and Mahli’s sons were Eleazar and Kish. Eleazar died with no sons, only daughters, so their cousins, the sons of Kish, married them.

questions.q: From what age did the Levites begin to do the work of the house of Yahweh?
questions.a: The Levites began to do the work from 20 years old and above.

questions.q: Why will the Levites no longer have to carry the tabernacle?
questions.a: Yahweh had given rest to his people, and he would live in Jerusalem forever, so the Levites would no longer need to carry the tabernacle from place to place.

questions.q: When did the officials count the Levites from 20 years old and above?
questions.a: They did this after David gave his last instructions, shortly before he died.

questions.q: What kind of work did the Levites do to help the priests?
questions.a: The Levites helped care for the courts and side rooms of the temple, purified the holy things, and prepared the bread, flour, wafers, and other items for the offerings.

questions.q: When did the Levites take time to thank and praise Yahweh?
questions.a: They praised him every morning and evening, when the priests offered burnt offerings, on the Sabbath, at the New Moon festivals, and at the other annual festivals.

questions.q: What three things did the Levites take care of?
questions.a: The Levites took care of the tent of meeting, the holy place, and the work of their relatives, the sons of Aaron, in the house of Yahweh.

commentary.text: Verses 1–23 David, having given charge concerning the building of the temple, settles the method of the temple service, and orders the officers of it. When those of the same family were employed together, it would engage them to love and assist one another.

Now the people of Israel were so many, there should be more employed in the temple service, that every Israelite who brought an offering might find a Levite ready to help him. When more work is to be done, it is pity but there should be more workmen. A new heart, a spiritual mind, which delights greatly in God's commandments, and can find a refreshing feast in his ordinances, forms the great distinction between the true Christian and all other men in the world. To the spiritual man every service will yield satisfaction. He will be ever abounding in the work of the Lord; being never so happy as when employed for such a good Master, in so pleasant a service. He will not regard whether he is called to take the lead, or to keep the charge of others who are placed over him. May we seek and serve the Lord uprightly, and leave all the rest to his disposal, by faith in his word.
